title: Cap. III Sol.: two guilty subjects — damning from crime does not prove electing from virtue
pass_a_gloss: Let us illustrate this which has been said by an example of this sort: Let us take two human beings guilty of robbery, or of treason against their Prince: The Prince therefore looks upon each as equally harmful: yet he wills to afflict one of them with capital death; he wills the other not only to absolve from punishment, but to admit into his household, and to heap with outstanding honors. Here if anyone should argue, The King condemned one of these from intuition of the crime committed, because namely he was both robber and traitor, therefore he elected the other to honors from intuition of innocence or virtue, because namely he was good and just; he would conclude falsely and ridiculously. Likewise therefore those also are deceived who from the intuition of sin in the will of damning argue to the intuition of merits in the will of freeing, and of electing to glory.
pass_b_english: Illustrate it so: take two men guilty of robbery or treason against their prince. The prince sees each as equally harmful — yet he wills to put one to death, and the other not only to free from punishment but to take into his household and heap with high honors. If someone argues The king condemned one from intuition of the crime (robber and traitor), therefore he elected the other to honors from intuition of innocence or virtue — that conclusion is false and ridiculous. So too are they deceived who from intuition of sin in the will to damn argue to intuition of merits in the will to free and elect to glory.
source_text: Illustremus hoc quod dictum est hujusmodi exemplo: Sumamus duos homines latrocinii, aut proditionis in Principem suum reos: Utrumque igitur ut ex aequo nocentem Princeps intuetur: vult tamen unum ex iis morte capitis afficere; vult alterum non modo a supplicio absolvere, sed in famulitium suum adsciscere, et honoribus eximiis cumulare. Hic siquis argutetur, Rex horum unum damnavit ex intuitu sceleris commissi, quia nempe et latro fuit et proditor, ergo alterum elegit ad honores ex intuitu innocentiae sive virtutis, quia scilicet bonus et justus erat; falso et ridicule concluserit. Perinde ergo et illi falluntur, qui ab intuitu peccati in voluntate damnandi arguunt ad intuitum meritorum in voluntate liberandi, et ad gloriam eligendi.
